# Agent contract 2

Normative agent contract distributed with the CMDS Zotero skill.
This document supersedes conflicting examples in the earlier WIP reference and ephemeral worker instructions.
Implementation status and test evidence belong in the plan, not in claims that examples have been executed.

## Scope

Fourteen CLI actions (`recent` and `import` since 0.5; `annotations` and `citing` since 0.6). Zotero remains read-only through documented Better BibTeX RPCs.
No database access, companion add-on, HTTP listener, telemetry, or automatic citekey changes.
The only write to non-plugin-owned notes is explicitly requested `reconcile --apply`; `import --apply` writes only
plugin-owned literature notes (new files, or managed sections of notes carrying this item's owner marker) and their
annotation images, through the same preview/apply path as the plugin UI.
Neither `identity` nor `cites` nor `locate` applies the Markdown it returns; `annotations` and `citing` only read.
Non-note writes are enumerated: (1) the private PDF text cache of `pdf-text`; (2) the bibliography sidecar of
`cites --bibliography --out` (0.5), by default `.cmds-zotero/bibliography/<slug>.<ext>` inside the plugin-owned
private folder, elsewhere only under the overwrite rule in "Bibliography formats and sidecars".

## Actions and envelope

| Action | Payload API version | Offline | Side effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| connection | 1 | Yes | Local BBT readiness probe only |
| info | 2 | Yes | None; no refresh or BBT probe |
| refresh | 1 | No | Explicit index/cache publication |
| resolve | 1 | Yes | None unless explicit `--refresh` |
| identity | 2 | Yes | None unless explicit `--refresh` |
| cites | 2 | Yes (`--format csl-json|bibtex|biblatex` and `--out` need the live host) | None; sidecar write with `--out` |
| reconcile | 2 | Dry-run only | Five-key hub update only with `--apply` |
| diagnostics | 1 | Yes (`--env` checks pdf.js, other vaults and the output folder only on the live host) | None; `--env` adds one BBT readiness probe on the live host |
| pdf-text | 2 | No | Private PDF text cache |
| locate | 2 | Yes | None |
| recent | 2 | No | None (Better BibTeX searches only) |
| import | 2 | No | Plugin-owned literature note and annotation images, only with `--apply` |
| annotations | 2 | Yes (`--fresh` and `--today` need the live host) | None (Better BibTeX reads only with `--fresh`/`--today`) |
| citing | 2 | Yes | None |

Every structured response has `apiVersion`, `contract: 2`, `apiVersions: [1,2]`, `action`, `vault`,
`ok`, `checkedAt` (UTC ISO timestamp), and `connection`. Failures add `reason` and `message`.
The service advertises API 2 while the four legacy action payloads retain API 1.
Legacy fields preserve their values/types; new envelope fields are additive, not a promise of identical whole-JSON bytes.

`connection` includes mode, Obsidian availability, plugin version/capabilities, BBT reachability,
index source/path/schema/generation/age/completeness/staleness/threshold, legacy-plugin state, and Git coverage.
Unknown is represented as unknown/null, never fabricated success. Ignored and already-tracked files are separate concerns.

BBT transport faults are classified once (0.5): `connection-refused` (any socket-level fault), `timeout`, `http-404`,
`http-other`, `aborted` (the plugin's own cancellation, never an observation about Zotero), `rpc` (a JSON-RPC error
envelope) and `invalid-response`. When the `connection` probe fails, `connection.bbt` carries `error` (human wording that
names the endpoint) and, when classified, `reason` from that vocabulary. `identity` and `cites` add
`bbtError {reason, endpoint}` beside `bibliographyReason`/`referencesReason: bbt-unreachable`, and a refused `refresh`
(forced or `ifOlderThanMinutes`) adds it beside its `reason`, only when the fault was a typed transport error.
`bibliographyReason`/`referencesReason: bbt-unreachable` remain the legacy coarse value for any failed BBT bibliography
call; when `bbtError` is present its `reason` is authoritative (`rpc`, `http-other` and `invalid-response` mean BBT
answered but the request failed). After a `connection-refused`, `timeout` or `http-404` fault, `cites` stops asking BBT
for the remaining keys. A reconcile apply refused because the evidence snapshot threw reports `refusedReason: index-invalid`
with `refusedMessage` (`bbt-unreachable` only for a typed transport error); a storage fault is never reported as a BBT outage.
The plugin's human status line derives freshness from the same `ageMinutes`/`stale` math and reports the last real BBT
call, so the UI and the CLI agree on freshness; its wording is UI copy, not part of this contract.

Bibliography text in `identity` and `cites` payloads may be served from the live plugin's write-through sidecar
(`.cmds-zotero/bibliography.json`, keyed by style, entry id, entry `contentHash` and Better BibTeX version) without a BBT
call (0.5); such text is byte-identical to what BBT rendered for that content hash and style, and the payload does not
distinguish it. `bibliographyReason: bbt-unreachable` with `bbtError` therefore means neither a live answer nor a cached
rendering existed. The sidecar is never filled at refresh time and the offline CLI never reads it.

Existing implicit refresh in read-only legacy operations is intentionally removed.
The read-only wrapper must not call an old host that might refresh on a read.
New CLI clients may use the offline core for old-host read-only capabilities; unsupported live writes fail explicitly.
No new flags may be silently discarded when talking to an old plugin.

### Setup checks: `diagnostics --env` (0.6.1)

`diagnostics --env` (request field `env: true`) adds `environment: {checks}` to the `diagnostics` payload, also to its
`index-missing`/`index-invalid` failure. Each check is `{id, status, title, detail, code?, paths?}` with `status` one of
`ok`, `info`, `warning`, `error` or `unknown` (not checked by this host), in this order: `zotero` (versions from a
readiness probe; the live host probes, the offline core reports `unknown`), `legacy-plugin`, `index`, `git`, `pdfjs`,
`peer-vaults` (whether each registered vault's note map can be read; names only), `output-folder` (notes in the literature
folder that no entry claims, and notes with Better Notes sync frontmatter; vault-relative `paths`, at most 20) and, when
the CLI tried the Obsidian bridge, `obsidian`. A check that needs attention carries a `code` from the diagnostic vocabulary
(`zotero-unreachable`, `zotero-reading-history-unavailable`, `legacy-plugin-enabled`, `index-missing`, `index-stale`,
`index-in-git`, `pdfjs-unavailable`, `peer-map-unreadable`, `better-notes-in-output`, `foreign-notes-in-output`,
`obsidian-unavailable`) and its status is that code's severity. The checks are report-only: nothing changes other plugins,
Git state or notes, and the `diagnostics` list itself is unchanged by `--env`. A host that does not list `diagnostics-env`
in `service.features` is refused before submission with `plugin-too-old`.

### Exit codes and transport

- `0`: structured usable results, including ambiguous, not-found, dry-run and diagnostics reports.
- `1`: `ok:false`, apply refusal/failure, legacy unavailable, or `--strict` with error-severity diagnostics.
- `2`: malformed arguments; plain stderr, no JSON.
- Structured errors appear exactly once on stdout, with one reason line on stderr.
- Repeat validation for direct API callers; a valid CLI parser is not a trust boundary.
- Read-only fallback is allowed before submission. Once accepted, or submission outcome is uncertain,
  never automatically resubmit or fall back. A timeout is not evidence that a write did not occur.
- Only explicit pre-acceptance capacity rejection retries, after 1, 2 and 4 seconds.
- Side-effect-free discovery reads may be retried on a transient bridge failure (empty CLI output) before
  submission; a CLI that cannot spawn or exits non-zero is immediate bridge loss. After submission, transient
  bridge failures (empty CLI output, transport errors) are retried until the deadline and then reported as timeout.

Jobs retain creation/completion timestamps. At most 16 unacknowledged jobs exist; `ackJob(id)` releases a
terminal job, so direct API callers acknowledge what they have read.
Completed/failed jobs expire after ten minutes; pending jobs are not evicted by that TTL.
A completed result persists until the client acknowledges it or its ten-minute TTL elapses; repeated reads
return the same result. Lost delivery is an uncertain outcome;
inspect the current state with read-only reconcile rather than automatically reapplying.
Unloading prevents late completion from recreating jobs or performing later writes.
A pending job is failed by the host after a per-action timeout (`pdf-text` 900 s, every other action 300 s); the job
carries `reason: timeout` and the CLI reports it as reason `timeout` (uncertain outcome, never resubmitted), not `requires-obsidian`; the
failure text names the action and the timeout, releases the write gate that blocks reconfiguration, and a late
settlement never reverses it. A timed-out write is an uncertain outcome like any other timeout and its failure text
says so; a timed-out read-only job says it left no state behind. The underlying work is not cancelled.

Failure `reason` values are derived from typed errors and the request first: an index refusal keeps its own reason;
a local-file refusal maps by code (`too-large` → `pdf-too-large`, any other → `pdf-invalid`), in the live host and
the offline CLI alike, so an oversized or non-PDF `--file` target is named precisely; a typed extraction failure maps
by code (`pdfjs-unavailable` → `pdfjs-unavailable`; unreadable, page-less, over-long or malformed → `pdf-invalid`;
text over the cache limit → `pdf-too-large`; a publication cancelled by a plugin reload → `invalid-request`);
`apply-failed` is reserved for a `reconcile` that was asked to write (`--apply`), while a failing dry-run or read
reports `invalid-request`. Only an untyped failure of `pdf-text`/`locate` is still classified by its wording, as a
last resort.
`locate --path` and `cites --path` resolve a note with or without its `.md` extension and treat a leading `/` as
vault-root-relative. A path that cannot lie inside the vault (scheme, `..`, `\`) is `path-outside-vault`. An
unknown note is `invalid-request` for `locate`; `cites` keeps reporting a path with no Markdown notes as
`path-outside-vault` (unchanged since 0.4).

## Identity and matching

`zoteroID` is a string such as `1:AAAA2345`, never a numeric database row ID.
Parent items, PDF attachments and annotations have distinct eight-character keys.
Selection URIs identify the parent; `zotero://open-pdf/.../items/BBBB2345?page=3` uses the attachment.
Group-library IDs and local library IDs are not interchangeable.

Hub fields are `citekey`, `doi`, `citekeyProvisional`, `zoteroID`, `zoteroSelectURI`,
`zoteroStatus`, and `zoteroCheckedAt`. The plugin may apply only the last five identity keys,
not `citekey` or `doi`. Existing plugin-owned literature-note fields remain supported.

Note references (`hub`, `raw`, `atoms`, `literatureNote`, `other`) carry `path`, `basename` and `uri`.
`vaultLinks` rows carry `vault`, `path` and `uri` (this vault's rows first, then each registered peer vault;
offline hosts return no rows plus a warning).
`uri` is the canonical Obsidian address `obsidian://open?vault=<vault>&file=<path without .md>` with both values
percent-encoded (`%20` for spaces, never `+`), the string Obsidian's own Copy Obsidian URL produces (Hookmark records
the same form; path-encoding parity with Hookmark is not verified). Peer-vault rows in `vaultLinks` use the Advanced
URI form `obsidian://advanced-uri?vault=<peer>&filepath=<path>.md` when that vault lists the plugin.
`obsidian://cmds-zotero` identity links are never emitted in note references.
### Literature-note frontmatter (0.5)

A literature note created by the plugin carries exactly `type: zotero` followed by `LITERATURE_IDENTITY_KEYS`
(`src/agent/types.ts`), in this order: `zoteroID`, `zoteroSelectURI`, `zotero-key`, `citekey`, `doi`, `title`,
`authors`, `year`, `tags`, then the display-parity group `zotero_title`, `zotero_author`, `zotero_year`,
`zotero_journal`, `zotero_doi`, `zotero_url`, `zotero_tags`.

- `zoteroID` is the only key agents may rely on. `zoteroSelectURI` carries the library scope (group items included).
  `zotero-key` is the ZotLit-compatible bare item key; it identifies an item only while the index holds one library.
  The `zotero_*` group mirrors the earlier CMDS template for display and carries no identity.
- Pre-0.5 vintage: frontmatter is written once and is user-owned afterwards, so notes created by 0.3/0.4 keep
  `zotero-id`, `zotero-library-id`, `zoteroItemKey`, `zoteroLibraryID`, `zoteroLibraryType` (and `zoteroGroupID`).
  These keys are never rewritten, never read as identity, and `reconcile` lists such notes as `type: literature`
  rows with the informational finding `legacy-frontmatter-dialect` (never apply-eligible). The rows are listed in
  `notes` but not counted in `scanned` ({hubs, rawSources, parseErrors}). `reconcile` and `diagnostics` surface the
  condition as one aggregated diagnostic per call (code `legacy-frontmatter-dialect`, severity `info`, `path` = the
  first sampled note; the message carries the count and up to 5 sample paths), not one diagnostic per note.
- Note identity ladder (note map, sidebars, "Update all", `vaultNotes`): `zoteroID`, then `zoteroSelectURI`, then
  `zotero-key` (single-library index only), then citekey/history equality — and citekey evidence counts only when the
  basename starts with `@` or `type` is one of `zotero`, `paper-hub`, `paper-analysis`, `raw-source`,
  `literature-zotero`; the output folder is never identity evidence. An explicit identity that names an item outside
  the index refuses the note rather than falling through. Notes carrying a foreign identity are never claimed on
  evidence weaker than `zoteroID`: a `bookendsID` or any other `type` is a hard marker, and a `bookends://` or
  `x-devonthink-item://` link in frontmatter marks only notes without a Zotero note `type` (a typed hub or raw source
  may link its PDF through DEVONthink and still resolves by citekey or DOI). Bookends auto-citekeys share the
  lastname+year shape of BBT keys.
- "Update all owned literature notes" treats a note as owned only when it resolves, lies inside the output folder and
  carries the owner marker; other linked notes are counted once (`Linked but not owned: M (not updated)`) and never
  trigger BBT.

- The vault citekey is the requested/existing hub key, never implicitly the current index key.
  DOI-only identity responses without a vault key omit `frontmatter.citekey`.
- Current/history matches are unioned by stable item identity. Collisions across different items are ambiguous.
- History may identify an item but does not prove that the vault key is pinned now.
- `citekeyProvisional:false` requires unambiguous identity and exact equality with the current BBT key.
  `zoteroStatus:resolved` plus `citekeyProvisional:true` is valid: registration exists, pinning is pending.
- Pin instruction: add `Citation Key: <requested-key>` to the Zotero item's Extra field manually.
- Resolve exactly one selector family: citekey, item-key plus library, DOI, arXiv, title, or query.
  Identity additionally accepts a vault citekey paired with one other lookup selector.
- DOI matching URL-decodes and normalizes case; emission preserves case. Keep one shared implementation.
- arXiv input must fully match a recognized identifier or arXiv URL, not an arbitrary URL substring.
- Author narrowing uses token boundaries. Exact normalized titles may resolve; prefixes/tokens/query rank only.
- Duplicate matches never select the first candidate. Multiple hubs return null plus a warning.
- Malformed YAML, unreadable notes and truncated discovery must be exposed, not silently treated as absent.

### Literature-note managed sections (0.5)

Generated sections of a literature note are delimited by `<!-- cmds-zotero:<id>:<sha256 of body> -->` and
`<!-- /cmds-zotero:<id> -->` (IDs: `overview`, `citation`, `metadata`, `notes`, `annotation-<attachment>-<annotation>`;
the set is closed). The variant `<!-- cmds-zotero:<id>:detached -->` … `<!-- /cmds-zotero:<id> -->` marks a block the
user has detached: agents must treat a detached block as user-owned text — never re-render, edit, re-hash or re-own
it, and never report it as edited or missing; only an explicit Reset chosen by the user replaces it (after the plugin
backs the note up under `.cmds-zotero/backups/notes/`). A managed block whose body no longer matches its hash is a
soft conflict (preserved verbatim; the rest of the note is still written); a missing, duplicate or damaged marker is a
hard conflict reported per ID with a line number, and the note is not written. Text after an opening marker on the
same line is moved below the block on the next update. Frontmatter stays outside the marker grammar and user-owned.

## Evidence availability

Absent, invalid, incomplete or unknown-age/future-dated indexes cannot establish absence.
A stale negative answer is withheld unless explicitly allowed, retaining the underlying verdict as `indexAnswer`.
`--allow-stale` does not make missing, malformed or incomplete evidence complete and never authorizes apply.
Positive identity evidence and source availability are separate from permission to write.

Vault-discovery incompleteness (notes skipped for malformed frontmatter, or a truncated scan) affects hub/raw
classification and reconcile apply, never the Zotero-index verdict: `resolve`/`identity` still return `not-found`
(`citekeyProvisional:true`) beside unrelated unparseable notes. Every such payload carries `scan {skipped, truncated}`
and a `vaultNotes.warnings` entry; truncated discovery (notes may be missing entirely) is reported as
`ok:false, reason: discovery-incomplete` with the skipped count and up to ten paths, while the index `status` stands.
`--allow-stale` addresses index age only and never lifts `discovery-incomplete`. Only the stale gate yields `stale-index`.

`cites` scans body and relevant frontmatter citations, unions canonical/history identities, and reports
resolved, hub-only, raw-only, dangling, ambiguous or unchecked. Hub/raw evidence is attached before any gate and
citekeys match exactly (case-preserving, as pandoc does), so provisional hub-only citations remain usable
when the Zotero index is stale or discovery is incomplete. Raw-only/dangling negative claims are withheld as
`unchecked` when evidence is insufficient, with `uncheckedReason: stale-index` (stale gate; `--allow-stale` lifts it)
or `discovery-incomplete` (skipped/truncated notes; repair them, `--allow-stale` does not apply); hints, diagnostics
and References lines name that cause. References output is deterministic and returned for review, not written into the note.

### Bibliography formats and sidecars (0.5)

A note's References section is any `##`–`######` heading whose title is one of the plugin setting
`referencesHeadings` (default `References`, `Bibliography`, `Works Cited`, `참고 문헌`, `참고 자료`; case-insensitive,
whitespace inside a title optional so `참고문헌` matches, an optional parenthesised qualifier of at most 40 characters,
optional closing hashes). The section ends at the next heading of the same or a higher level. Each file reports
`referencesSection.heading` (the heading line as written) beside `present`/`listed`. The offline CLI reads the same
setting from the vault's plugin data; an empty or malformed setting keeps the defaults.

`cites --bibliography` takes `--format text|markdown|csl-json|bibtex|biblatex` (default `text`, unchanged behaviour).
`references.format` names the format. `text`/`markdown` keep `resolved`, `unresolved`, `markdown` (the References
block, whose first line reuses the found heading, else `## References`) and add `style`, `heading` and `content`
(`text`: resolved entries separated by blank lines; `markdown`: the block). They still work offline from hub full
citations (`referencesReason: offline` when index entries could not be rendered).
The structured formats run one BBT `item.export` per Zotero library (`Better CSL JSON`, `Better BibTeX`,
`Better BibLaTeX`) over the resolved keys, exporting each entry under its current citekey; the payload carries
`content` (CSL-JSON: one merged plain array, `abstract` and `note` removed and listed in `stripped`, `id` and
`citation-key` kept; BibTeX/BibLaTeX: texts concatenated), `exported` (ids / entry keys present), `unresolved` (every
cited key without an export entry, with `citeStatus` and a hint; a resolved key the export omitted is listed with
`citeStatus: resolved`) and `renamed` (`{cited, current}` for keys matched through `citekeyHistory`, which pandoc
cannot match to the exported `id`). Structured formats need the live host: the offline core answers
`referencesReason: offline` with `content: null`; a typed BBT fault is `referencesReason: bbt-unreachable` plus
`bbtError`, an unusable export payload `export-invalid`. No `item.bibliography` call is made for structured formats.

`--out [path]` writes the bibliography (live host only; `requires-obsidian` otherwise, and `ingest-ro.mjs` rejects the
flag). Without a value the path is `.cmds-zotero/bibliography/<slug>.<json|bib|md|txt>` — the slug is the note
basename without `.md`, the folder name for folder targets, `vault` for the root; characters `\ / : * ? " < > |` and
control characters are dropped, whitespace becomes `-`. The write ensures `.cmds-zotero/.gitignore` first. An explicit
path must be vault-relative (no scheme, `\`, `..`, empty segments; `path-outside-vault` otherwise). Overwrite rule:
under `.cmds-zotero/bibliography/` the plugin owns the file; elsewhere the target must be absent or start with the
generator marker line the plugin writes (`% cmds-zotero bibliography` for `.bib`, `<!-- cmds-zotero bibliography -->`
for `.md`/`.txt`; CSL-JSON stays a plain array and carries no marker, so an existing JSON file needs `--force`); a
Markdown note that lacks the marker is never replaced, `--force` included. A refused write is `ok:false,
reason: invalid-request` with the bibliography still in the payload. The response carries
`out: {path, written, bytes?}`. A `cites` request with `out` holds the plugin's write gate like `reconcile --apply`.

## Reconcile transition contract

Discovery is by frontmatter type; folders only narrow it. Raw sources are report-only.
`type: zotero` literature notes appear only when they carry pre-0.5 keys (`legacy-frontmatter-dialect`, report-only;
listed in `notes`, not counted in `scanned`).
The Raw Sources root is never writable even if a file is mislabeled paper-hub.
ID/URI/key/history/folder/DOI/arXiv can contribute identity evidence, but precedence never overrides a contradiction.
Present-but-invalid fields retain their presence: null, empty strings, wrong types and duplicate keys are not absent.
Conflicting identities, malformed fields, ambiguous results and unchecked evidence produce no automatic patch.

| Field | Allowed transition |
| --- | --- |
| zoteroID / zoteroSelectURI | Absent to validated value; existing values never overwritten or deleted |
| zoteroStatus | Absent to resolved or fresh not-found; not-found/unavailable/ambiguous to resolved; unavailable/ambiguous to fresh not-found |
| citekeyProvisional | Absent to boolean; true to false only when current key is exactly pinned; false is never reversed |
| zoteroCheckedAt | Written only alongside a material authorized change to another allowed field |

Existing identity evidence prevents an automatic negative transition. Resolved status never downgrades.
Malformed identities require human repair followed by a new dry-run; no repair action is added in 0.4.
S01 corrections are suggestions only; reconcile does not edit the body.

Scan policy (0.6, R8). `reconcile` reports `scan {skipped, truncated, skippedDetail, parseErrors}`: `skippedDetail`
gives each skipped path its kind (`unreadable`, `parse-error`, `symlink` for the offline reader) and `parseErrors` lists
every note whose frontmatter did not parse. `--apply` is refused vault-wide (`reason: scan-incomplete`, the message
names up to ten paths, `apply.refusedMessage` repeats it) for a truncated scan, any unreadable or symlinked entry, or a
parse-error note inside the `--folders` scope. A parse-error note elsewhere no longer vetoes the apply; the host reads
it once, and a hub whose citekey it mentions (word-bounded) is withheld individually with the finding
`blocked-by-parse-error` (`skippedReason: blocked-by-parse-error`, `blockedBy` = the paths, `proposed: null`) until it is
repaired, because that note may be the hub's own atom or S01 note. A parse-error note that vanished after the listing
counts as unreadable.

### Apply protocol

Require live host, valid complete fresh index, current BBT reachability and explicitly disabled legacy plugin.
Unknown preconditions fail closed. Serialize applies per canonical vault/path.
Bind each proposal to its source snapshot (the SHA-256 of the note text); re-read and check the source before writing.

The write is a line patch (0.6, R8) of the whole note text inside one read-modify-write callback (`vault.process`).
The callback rechecks the plugin lifecycle, evidence freshness and the source hash, then replaces the single column-0
line of each changed allowed key (a trailing comment on that line is kept) and appends missing keys before the closing
fence in `HUB_WRITABLE_KEYS` order. Every other byte stays: comments, quoting style, folded scalars, lists, trailing
whitespace, CRLF, BOM and the body. A value is written bare only when YAML 1.1 and 1.2 parsers both read it back as
the same string (letters, digits and `_ . / : @ % + ~ -`, not a boolean, null, number or timestamp); anything else is
double-quoted with JSON escapes, so a backslash becomes `\\`, and DEL, C1 controls, U+2028/U+2029 and the BOM become
`\uXXXX`. The patched text must parse back to the intended frontmatter (non-allowed keys and unchanged allowed keys
equal, changed keys at their proposed values) before it is handed to the writer. Hand-formatted YAML that a
parse/stringify pass would rewrite is patched like any other hub; dry-run rows may carry the informational
`yamlNormalisable` (live host only) and it never withholds a proposal.
A hub whose current allowed value is a block scalar, flow collection, multi-line or unterminated quoted scalar, a key
that appears twice or in quoted form, or a proposed value that is neither string nor boolean is skipped with
`skippedReason: frontmatter-not-patchable` and nothing is written (0.5's `yaml-roundtrip-unsafe` no longer occurs).
A source change before the write or inside the callback is skipped as `changed-since-plan` with `wrote: false`, never an
integrity failure: a throw from the callback means the writer received no text, whatever another editor did meanwhile.
Verify body bytes, non-allowed values and intended allowed values afterward, even after a possibly post-write exception.
No-op runs do not update timestamps. Per-file failures and actual writes are reported distinctly; `apply.notes[]`
add `replacedKeys` and `appendedKeys` (which of `changedKeys` replaced a line and which were appended).
`apply.notes[].wrote` is `null` when a post-invocation read cannot establish the outcome; this is an integrity failure,
not proof of no write. Top-level note `applied` flags mirror successful writer outcomes. Revalidation may advance
`zoteroCheckedAt` while preserving the approved material patch. Each queued file rechecks evidence and the callback
rejects evidence that has expired before assignments.

The public API does not provide whole-file compare-and-swap against external editors.
Do not claim complete atomicity or automatically roll back over concurrent edits.
A verification mismatch is an integrity failure with actual-write/churn accounting, not a successful skip.
Stop further writes after integrity failure and let the user inspect current state.

## Recently read papers and literature-note import (0.5)

`recent` lists the papers whose PDF Zotero opened in its reader within `--days` (1–365; default the plugin setting
`recentReadsDays`, 30), newest first. Zotero 10 records `attachmentLastRead` (local calendar day granularity in search);
Better BibTeX `item.search` with `[["resultLevel","item"],["lastRead","isInTheLast","N days"]]` maps the attachment-level
condition to the parent item, and exact-day probes `["lastRead","is","YYYY-MM-DD"]` (local date) date each paper. Neither
the BetterBibTeX JSON export nor `item.attachments` carries `lastRead`. Rows without a citekey (standalone PDFs) are omitted.
Each item reports `citekey`, `id` (`libraryID:itemKey`, null when unreadable), `itemKey`, `libraryType`, `groupID`,
`library`, `title`, `year`, `authors`, `readOn` (local day or null), `readLabel`, `inIndex`, `fresh` (read from Zotero now,
not the saved index), `note` and optional `problem`. `note` is `{state, path, missing, orphaned, annotations, summary,
needsImport}` with `state` one of `none`, `behind` (Zotero has annotations without a block in the note), `current`,
`foreign` (a note has the identity but not this plugin's owner marker; never written) and `duplicate`. It compares the
note's `annotation-<attachment>-<annotation>` markers (detached blocks included) with the item's annotations; `orphaned`
counts blocks whose annotation was deleted in Zotero, which are kept, never removed. Zotero unreachable is `ok:false,
reason: bbt-unreachable` with `bbtError`. A Zotero older than 10 refuses the reading-history search: that is `ok:false,
reason: zotero-too-old` (0.6), never `bbt-unreachable`.

`import` takes exactly one selector (`--citekey`, or `--item-key` with `--library`) and is a dry run unless `--apply`.
It renders from the item as Zotero has it now (one `item.export` plus `item.attachments`; the saved index is not
rewritten), so annotations made since the last refresh are included; a citekey renamed in Zotero is followed by item key
and an export that resolves to another item is refused. A citekey the saved index does not know yet is looked up with an
exact `citationKey` search (several libraries using it is `invalid-request`). When the item cannot be read fresh the
request is refused (`bbt-unreachable` or `invalid-request`) unless `--allow-stale`, which renders from the saved index and
adds a warning; a first import still needs bibliography text (0.5 R12). The payload carries `dryRun`, `item`, `fresh`,
`note {path, existed, before, after?}` (note states as in `recent`), `preview {conflicts, softConflicts, sections (counts by
state), changes}`, `outcome {status: created|updated|unchanged|refused, path, preserved, message?, summary}` (null on a dry
run) and `warnings`. Edited generated sections are soft conflicts: kept verbatim and listed in `preserved` while the rest of
the note is written. Hard conflicts (unowned note, damaged or duplicate markers, several notes with one identity, a note
changed between preview and write) are `ok:false, reason: note-conflict`, in a dry run as well as on apply. A failure while
writing maps to `apply-failed`. The user-owned regions of a literature note are the frontmatter (initialised once), the
`## Synthesis` callout, `## Notes`, any text outside managed markers and detached blocks; an agent records its own synthesis
there, never inside `<!-- cmds-zotero:<id>:<hash> -->` blocks.

The live host advertises its action list (`service.actions`); the CLI refuses `recent`, `import`, `annotations` and `citing`
against a host that does not list them with `plugin-too-old` before submitting anything (the message names the plugin version
that added the action, and for an offline-capable action suggests `--offline`). `recent` and `import` are live-only; offline
they answer `requires-obsidian`. `ingest-ro.mjs` allows `recent` and `import` dry runs and still rejects `--apply`; it allows
`annotations` and `citing` entirely, because neither writes.

## Annotations and citing for agents (0.6)

Both actions are additive to contract 2: an older host does not list them (see above) and every existing action is unchanged.

### `annotations`

`annotations` returns the annotations of one paper in Zotero's reading order (attachments as listed, each attachment's
annotations by `annotationSortIndex`). Selector: exactly one of `--citekey` (a former key resolves and reports
`matchedHistory: true`), `--item-key` with `--library`, or `--today`. Filters (all optional, combinable, all applied to the
annotations of the selected item): `--color` (a palette name `yellow|red|green|blue|purple|magenta|orange|gray`, matched by
the nearest palette hue, or a hex value such as `#ffd400`), `--type` (`highlight|underline|note|text|image|ink`), `--tag`
(case-insensitive, exact) and `--attachment KEY` (one attachment of the item; a key the item does not have is
`invalid-request` and the response lists the item's attachments). An unknown color or type is `invalid-request`. The selector
outcomes are those of `resolve`: `status` is `resolved`, `ambiguous` (the same citekey in two libraries; `ranked` lists them and
no annotations are returned) or `not-found`; a `not-found` verdict from a stale index is withheld as `ok:false, reason:
stale-index` unless `--allow-stale`.

Freshness. By default the answer is a snapshot of the saved index (`source: snapshot`, `fresh: false`, `annotationsAsOf` the
index's `generatedAt`; a warning is added when the index is stale, because annotations made since then are missing) and works
offline. `--fresh` (live host only) reads the item as Zotero has it now (one `item.export` plus `item.attachments`, the same
read `import` uses; `source: fresh`, `annotationsAsOf` the request time) without touching the saved index. If Zotero cannot
answer, the request fails (`bbt-unreachable` with `bbtError` for a typed transport fault, else `invalid-request`) and
returns no annotations; with `--allow-stale` it answers from the saved index instead, with `source: snapshot` and a
warning. Offline, `--fresh` and `--today` are `requires-obsidian`; the snapshot is never substituted silently. `item.attachments`
may make Zotero render a missing image-annotation cache file into its own cache folder; the library is not changed.

`--today` selects the paper Zotero opened on the current local calendar day (the `lastRead` search of `recent`, live only;
a Zotero older than 10 is `reason: zotero-too-old`, as for `recent`). It
resolves only when exactly one paper qualifies: none is `status: not-found`, several are `status: ambiguous` with `candidates`
(`citekey`, `itemKey`, `libraryType`, `groupID`, `library`, `title`, `year`, `authors`, `readOn`, `id`, `inIndex`) and no
annotations; the response carries `today {day, reads}`. A paper the saved index does not know is `ok:false, reason: stale-index`
unless `--fresh` reads it from Zotero by its reading-history row.

Payload: `status`, `matchedBy`, `query` (or `today`), `item` (`id`, `itemKey`, `libraryID`, `libraryType`, `groupID`,
`citekey`, `citekeyHistory`, `title`, `authors`, `year`, `doi`, `zoteroSelectURI`), `source`, `fresh`, `annotationsAsOf`,
`filters` (as given), `summary {total, matched, attachments, byType, byColor}` (`total` counts every annotation of the item,
the rest the filtered set), `attachments` and `warnings`. Each attachment has `key`, `title`, `openURI`, `contentType`,
`annotationCount` (before the type, color and tag filters) and `annotations`; attachments without a matching annotation are
left out. Each annotation has `key`, `attachmentKey`, `type`, `color {name, hex}` (`name` null when the hue is unknown),
`page` (one-based physical position), `pageLabel` (the printed label), `text`, `comment`, `tags`, `uri` (the
`zotero://open-pdf/…?page=N&annotation=KEY` link, built on the ATTACHMENT key), `sortIndex` and `dateModified`. An image
annotation adds `image {cachePath, private: true, vaultCopies}`: `cachePath` is a local path inside Zotero's cache and
`private: true` marks it as never to be committed, published or pasted into shared notes; `vaultCopies` lists the copies the
literature import made in the image folder (`<imageFolder>/<libraryType>-<library>-<attachmentKey>-<annotationKey>-<sha256>.<ext>`;
several when the image changed, empty when it was never imported). The image folder is read only when an image annotation is
listed. What a live reader would add (the open tab or the selected annotation) is not available: Better BibTeX exposes
neither.

### `citing`

`citing` lists the vault notes that cite one Zotero item. Selector: exactly one family, as `resolve` takes it (`--citekey`,
`--item-key` with `--library`, `--doi`, `--arxiv`, `--title` or `--query`, with `--year`/`--author` narrowing a title or
query). Outcomes are those of `resolve` (`ambiguous` and `not-found` return no notes; a stale `not-found` is withheld as
`stale-index` unless `--allow-stale`). The keys searched are the item's current citekey and its former keys
(`keys.searched`, each `{key, kind: current|former}`). A key another item also carries, as its current or a former citekey
(for example the same key in a group library, or a former key a later item reused), cannot be attributed to this item and is
left out and reported in `keys.excluded` (`reason: shared`, `sharedWith` up to five `{id, citekey, libraryID}`); when every key
is excluded the vault is not scanned, and `scan` says so (`performed: false`, `complete: false`), so the empty `notes` list
proves nothing.

A note is scanned exactly as `cites` scans it, so the two actions agree on what a citation is. Counted in the body: Pandoc
`[@key]` (with locators, prefixes and `;`-separated groups), narrative `@key`, suppressed-author `-@key` and wikilinks
`[[@key]]` / `[[@key|alias]]` (the `form` field says `pandoc`, `bare` or `wikilink`). Counted in the frontmatter, and reported
apart as `frontmatter` rows `{key, field, form}`: bare keys in `cites`, `supports` and `counters`, and `[@key]` tokens inside
`evidenceFor`, `evidenceAgainst`, `sourceCallout` and `hypotheses`. Not counted: occurrences inside fenced code blocks (``` or
~~~), the frontmatter text itself when scanning the body, e-mail-like tokens (`name@key.org`), a note's own frontmatter
`citekey`, wikilinks and bare `@key` inside frontmatter values, a different key that merely starts with the searched one, and
everything inside the note's References section (the bibliography, not a citation; the section is found with the plugin
setting `referencesHeadings`, as in `cites`).

Payload: `status`, `matchedBy`, `query`, `item`, `keys {searched, excluded}`, `notes`, `summary {notes, listed, citations,
frontmatterCitations, scanned, truncated}` and `scan {skipped, truncated, complete}`. Each note has `path`, `basename`, `uri`
(the canonical `obsidian://open` address), `count` (all citations, frontmatter included), `frontmatterCount`, `citations`
(body citations in note order: `key`, one-based `line` and `column` over the note text as read, `form`, and `excerpt`, the
line cut to at most 120 characters around the citation with `…` marking a cut end) and `frontmatter`. Notes are ordered by
`count` (most first), then by path. Output is bounded: at most 20 body citations per note (`positionsTruncated: true`; `count`
stays exact) and 500 notes (`summary.truncated: true`; `summary.notes` stays exact). Notes are read with bounded concurrency
(8). An unreadable note, or one whose frontmatter did not parse, is listed in `scan.skipped` and sets `scan.complete: false`: an
empty or short `notes` list proves absence only when `scan.complete` is true. A truncated vault listing (more than 20,000 notes)
is `ok:false, reason: discovery-incomplete` with the notes found so far still reported.

## PDF evidence and private caches

Use the bundled public `loadPdfJs()` API and guarded local reads, not a new PDF service. Pass Obsidian's bundled
pdf.js resources (`cMapUrl: "/lib/pdfjs/cmaps/"`, `cMapPacked: true`, `standardFontDataUrl: "/lib/pdfjs/standard_fonts/"`,
the URLs its own viewer uses) so CID-keyed CJK fonts and non-embedded standard fonts extract.
`pdf-text` adds `textLayer {textLayer: full|partial|none, emptyPages, bodyChars, ocrRecommended}`: lines repeated on at
least half of the pages (three or more pages) are watermarks or running heads, not body text, and a page under 20 body
characters has none. `none` or `partial` adds a warning to run OCR (not part of this plugin); `locate` cannot verify
quotes in such pages.
Capture the input byte length before passing a transferable buffer to pdf.js.
Page is one-based physical position; pageLabel is printed text. Empty/dash-only labels fall back to position.
`p.-` must never appear. Fuzzy/ambiguous/unverified matches must not masquerade as confirmed quote locations.

Cache names bind source scope and content hash: `<libraryType>-<libraryID>-<attachmentKey>-<sha16>.json` for
Zotero attachments and `file-<pathHash16>-<sha16>.json` for vault PDFs, where the path hash is the SHA-256 of the
normalized vault-relative path (`./`, leading, trailing and repeated `/` ignored, so `./A/x.pdf` and `A/x.pdf` name
one cache). Attachment and vault-file caches cannot select/evict each other, and two vault PDFs with
identical bytes at different paths keep separate caches. Pre-0.5 `file-<sha16>.json` names are foreign: never
selected, never evicted; re-run `pdf-text` to rebuild.
Validate schema, source identity, file scope, page order/uniqueness, limits and metadata before use.
A changed PDF is verification failure; an unavailable original is unchecked. Preserve truncation warnings on cache hits.
Always clean up pdf.js tasks/documents on failure or completion.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| PDF input | 64 MiB / 2,000 pages |
| Text per page | 200,000 characters, explicit truncation warning |
| Inline text response | 200 KB total |
| Quote | 8 KiB |
| Serialized cache read/write | 32 MiB; refuse unreadable oversized cache output |
| Markdown | 2 MiB |
| Citation folder walk | 2,000 files, report truncation |
| Vault discovery | 20,000 notes, report omissions/truncation |

Private data lives under `.cmds-zotero/`; ensure a protective `.cmds-zotero/.gitignore` before writing.
Index paths and full-paper caches are sensitive. Ignore rules do not untrack files or erase published history.
Never include real library exports, source PDFs, private paths or session identifiers in public fixtures/docs.

## Acceptance gates

Contract fixtures cover every action, API version, exit code and unsupported host capability.
Tests cover malformed/contradictory identities, all transitions, history/current collisions, parser failures,
stale/incomplete snapshots, queued edits, lifecycle changes, read-only behavior, cache boundaries and detached buffers.
The offline bundle must derive from current source and contain no runtime Obsidian import.
Full lint/typecheck/tests/build, public-source sanitization and release version checks run before release approval.
Live installation, user-hub apply, commits, pushes and releases require their own authorization.
